summary: A file of 256 MiB on ext2 and on exFAT, a mebibyte astride the 4 GiB line of a sparse ext2 file, a write past each format's limit refused by name, and an ext2 file of 256 MiB read twice through the file page cache with every way of changing a file seen by the next read, on volumes that the host's own tools make in an empty AHCI disk and check after the machine; the program is tests/cases/machine/large_scenario.c, which runs tests/bigfileprobe.c and tests/musl/pagecachemusl.c at the kernel's debug shell

cases.behavior: a 256 MiB file on a 6 GiB ext2 volume that mke2fs made is written, sized, sought, read at its middle and near its end, shared between a second open and a duplicate, truncated in a few disk commands and appended to, and read back whole after a remount in a second boot; a mebibyte written astride the 4 GiB line of a sparse file reads back with its hole zero; a write at the file limit for 4096-byte blocks is refused with EFBIG and named in the kernel's log; and e2fsck -fn finds the volume consistent after the machine

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machines and removes the empty disk, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: write the disk's MBR, with identity 1a26e001 and its ext2, exFAT and FAT32 partitions, with mkmbr, and make the ext2 volume in the first with mke2fs; the disk stays sparse
boot the test image on the disk, run bigfileprobe write at the debug shell and end the machine
boot the test image on the disk again and run bigfileprobe verify, which reads the file back after the new mount
run bigfileprobe sparse, which writes and reads a mebibyte astride the 4 GiB line of a new file
run bigfileprobe limit at the file limit for 4096-byte blocks
end the machine and run e2fsck -fn on the volume

assertions.checks: mkmbr writes the disk's table and mke2fs makes the 6 GiB ext2 volume in its first partition, each exiting 0

bigfileprobe write says BIGFILE OK (write) and never BIGFILE FAIL: the file of 256 MiB written and synced, its size, a seek to its end and back, its blocks at the middle and near the end, an offset shared with a duplicate and not with a second open, a truncate to three quarters that takes at most 8 disk commands for each 4 MiB it frees and 64 more, and an appended mebibyte read back
bigfileprobe verify, in a second boot, returns to the debug shell with status 0, by the kernel's record of its exit
bigfileprobe verify says BIGFILE OK (verify) and never BIGFILE FAIL: after the new mount the file has the size the write left, every block has its number and a read at its end gives nothing
bigfileprobe sparse returns to the debug shell with status 0, by the kernel's record of its exit

bigfileprobe sparse says BIGFILE OK (sparse) and never BIGFILE FAIL: a mebibyte written astride the 4 GiB line of a new file sets its size past the line, reads back, leaves the hole below it reading zeros, and the file truncates to a block past the line
bigfileprobe limit at offset 2196873666560 returns to the debug shell with status 0, by the kernel's record of its exit
bigfileprobe limit says BIGFILE OK (limit) and never BIGFILE FAIL: a one-byte write at the file limit for 4096-byte blocks is refused with EFBIG and the file stays empty
the kernel's log says ext2: write: offset 2095101 MiB is past the file limit of 2095101 MiB for 4096-byte blocks
e2fsck -fn on the volume after the machine exits 0, finding it consistent
